lateral_torso_line_topology.vertical_line_count_and_spacing: 4 primary high-contrast vertical lines visible on the lateral torso. Spacing is irregular, with a wider gap between the second and third lines (approx. 20% of torso width) compared to others (approx. 10-12%).
lateral_torso_line_topology.intersection_coordinates_bifurcations: One visible Y-shaped bifurcation on the second line from the shoulder, located at approximately mid-latitudinal torso height where the line splits into two distinct paths moving ventrally.
lateral_torso_line_topology.discontinuity_mapping: The third vertical line from the shoulder is discontinuous, terminating abruptly at mid-flank and resuming as a shorter segment near the ventral fringe.

posterior_constellation_clusters.spatial_cluster_density: A cluster of 4 distinct high-contrast white spots is visible on the lower haunch. Density is concentrated in a 40x40 pixel region relative to the hind limb junction.
posterior_constellation_clusters.linear_blob_alignment: Two spots on the posterior flank align horizontally to form a semi-connected geometric line segment parallel to the ventral fringe.

macro_horn_vector_geometry.curve_trajectory_2d: Horns follow a spiral-lyrate trajectory, initiating at an approx. 50-degree lateral angle from the pedicle before curving medially toward the terminal tips.
macro_horn_vector_geometry.apical_span_ratio: The pixel distance between terminal tips is approximately 2.5 times the width of a single horn base.
macro_horn_vector_geometry.terminal_contrast_ratio: Ivory-colored tipping (high-contrast pixels) accounts for approximately 15% of the total visible horn length from base to apex.

other_distinctive_markers: Presence of four Red-billed oxpeckers (Buphagus erythrorhynchus) attached to the lateral torso and upper neck. Prominent white dorsal crest extending from the nape through the lumbar region.
